meeting_header: Recorded: 2027-10-19 16:00 PDT | Duration: ~45 mins | Attendees: Claire Park (Redwood AE), Ravi Menon (Redwood SE), Marta Gomez (CTO - Nebula), Ethan Browne (VP Eng - Nebula), Priya Shah (Head of MLOps - Nebula), Liam O'Connell (Security Lead - Nebula)
summary: Kickoff for Nebula Health onboarding to Redwood. Covered success criteria (latency <200ms p95, data residency, SOC2), deployment options (hosted vs dedicated vs private VPC), pilot scope (subset of inference traffic, 2 models), and next steps (pricing, security docs, technical deep-dive). Customer requested private deployment reference arch and explicit compliance artifacts.
topics: Deployment options: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private
transcript:
[00:00] Claire Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Claire from Redwood. Quick intro, Ravi and I will run through the onboarding plan and figure out pilot scope.
[00:12] Marta Gomez: Hi, Marta here, CTO at Nebula. Thanks all.
[00:16] Ethan Browne: Ethan, VP Eng. We'll be driving the infra side.
[00:20] Priya Shah: Priya, MLOps, will own the model footprint and deployment testing.
[00:24] Liam O'Connell: Liam, security. I'll be asking a lot of questions about encryption and audit logs.
[00:30] Ravi Menon: Quick agenda, why Redwood, what onboarding looks like, pilot definition, and then action items. Sound good?
[00:36] Marta Gomez: Yep.
[00:40] Claire Park: High level - Nebula told us the two main things are predictable latency under 200ms p95 and keeping PHI off the hosted plane, is that right?
[00:50] Priya Shah: Correct. We have some PHI in annotations, so we need either private deployment or dedicated with strict network controls.
[00:58] Ethan Browne: Our main traffic is inference for triage suggestions - bursts during clinic hours, peaks around 800 qps internal, avg 250.
[01:08] Ravi Menon: Great, that helps. For pilot we usually recommend starting with a small slice: 2 models, the triage model and a smaller reranker. We can run those on Dedicated or Private - both are supported.
[01:22] Liam O'Connell: On security, we need SOC2 Type II, encryption at rest with customer-managed KMS, SSO via SAML, and audit logs retained for one year. Is Redwood able to support all that?
[01:34] Claire Park: Yes, we offer SOC2, KMS integrations, SAML/SSO, and audit logs. We'll share the security package. For Private deployments we can keep the control plane inside your VPC or on-prem, that addresses PHI concerns.
[01:48] Marta Gomez: What's the delta in effort between Dedicated vs Private? We want to understand time to pilot and risk.
[01:56] Ravi Menon: Dedicated is fastest - we provision a dedicated GPU pool for you, network isolation, but the control plane stays hosted. Private requires VPC peering or on-prem setup, more infra work but gives full control. For timelines: dedicated pilot can be up in 2-3 weeks after contract; private usually 4-8 weeks depending on network and approvals.
[02:18] Ethan Browne: That 800 qps peak - does Redwood support autoscaling for bursts without manual intervention?
[02:24] Ravi Menon: Yes, autoscaling and burst policies can be configured. We also do KV/prefix caching that reduces repeated token costs if you have repeat prompts.
[02:34] Priya Shah: About model versions - we need to pin specific weights for validation. Can we pin and do canary rollouts?
[02:41] Claire Park: Absolutely, pin model versions and do canaries/A-B rollouts. Rollback is automatic if a regression is detected based on request-level monitoring.
[02:54] Liam O'Connell: Audit logs - what granularity? We need token-level access logs and admin activity logs.
[03:01] Ravi Menon: We capture request metadata, route, model version, and admin actions. For token-level visibility we have cost breakdowns per token but we don't store raw PII unless configured. We'll provide the exact schema in the security doc.
[03:17] Marta Gomez: Pricing - ballpark numbers for Dedicated vs Private?
[03:22] Claire Park: We'll send a pricing sheet. Dedicated is commit-based monthly; private has a platform fee + infra. Claire: action item to send the sheet.
[03:33] Ethan Browne: For the pilot, we'd like realistic benchmarks run on our traffic profile. Is there a way to run a short benchmark with sample logs?
[03:40] Ravi Menon: Yes, if Priya can provide a representative trace or synthetic workload we'll run a head-to-head on latency and cost estimates. That usually takes 3-5 business days.
[03:52] Priya Shah: I can pull a 48-hour sample and masked logs. We'll need guidance on what to mask.
[03:58] Liam O'Connell: Masking rules: remove PHI fields, hash IDs, preserve timing distribution is most important.
[04:06] Claire Park: We'll share a masking guide and reference script.
[04:10] Marta Gomez: Any gotchas with the private deployment - do we need dedicated networking peering approvals or specific ports?
[04:17] Ravi Menon: We'll send reference architecture with ports and security groups. In our experience, the biggest delays are firewall change approvals and procurement for dedicated hardware if you choose on-prem.
[04:28] Ethan Browne: How do we handle secrets/KMS keys in private? Customer-managed keys?
[04:34] Claire Park: You can bring your own keys via supported KMS/HSM integrations; on Private we can also do full key control inside your KMS.
[04:42] Priya Shah: Ops question - what's the observability like? We need per-model latency distributions, token cost, and tracing to our internal APM.
[04:50] Ravi Menon: Redwood Console exposes per-route dashboards, latency histograms, token breakdowns, and tracing hooks you can forward to Datadog or New Relic.
[04:59] Marta Gomez: Timeline - we want pilot live inside November, ideally early November. Is that realistic?
[05:06] Claire Park: If we commit this week and go Dedicated, early November is doable. For Private maybe later in November or December depending on approvals.
[05:16] Ethan Browne: Procurement - who signs the contract on Redwood side?
[05:20] Claire Park: I'll be AE handling the contract; legal can engage once we share terms. We'll include SLA language for Dedicated.
[05:28] Liam O'Connell: On data residency - our data must remain in the US east region. Can we pin region?
[05:34] Ravi Menon: Yes, routing and region pinning are supported, we'll include region options in the architecture doc.
[05:42] Priya Shah: For the runbook and playbooks - will CSM provide onboarding sessions?
[05:47] Claire Park: Yes, you will have a dedicated CSM for post-contract onboarding and weekly syncs.
[05:52] Marta Gomez: Any limitations with model size and quantization if we push for low-latency?
[05:58] Ravi Menon: We recommend certain quantization profiles per model; for ultra-low latency we can use optimized kernels and batching configurations. We'll propose tradeoffs in the performance doc.
[06:08] Ethan Browne: Can we do a short smoke test before the pilot - like 10k requests to validate end-to-end?
[06:13] Ravi Menon: Yes, a smoke run is standard. We'll coordinate windows to avoid affecting production traffic.
[06:19] Priya Shah: Who will be the daily contact for infra issues during the pilot?
[06:23] Claire Park: Ravi will be SE point, and your CSM will handle coordination.
[06:28] Liam O'Connell: Is there an incident playbook if there's a security event?
[06:32] Ravi Menon: Yes, we'll share incident response procedures and SLA escalation paths.
[06:37] Marta Gomez: Okay let's recap next steps.
[06:40] Claire Park: Recap: Claire send pricing and Dedicated vs Private comparison; Ravi send private deployment reference arch and checklist; Priya provide traffic samples; Liam supply compliance requirements; schedule technical deep-dive.
[06:54] Ethan Browne: Sounds good.
[06:56] Priya Shah: I'll get the logs and SLOs over by the 25th.
[06:59] Liam O'Connell: I'll compile the compliance list and timeline.
[07:04] Claire Park: Great - thanks everyone. We'll follow up over email and add the docs to the shared folder.
[07:10] Marta Gomez: Thanks all.
[07:12] Claire Park: End.

Note: transcript has some minor transcription errors and dropped words consistent with automated call transcription (e.g., 'qps' may appear as 'q p s', some product names slightly off).
